what_happened.line: The Finance Committee heard the town manager's FY20 preliminary budget, covering revenues, state aid, expenditures, new positions, reserves and the capital plan.
Members and a resident discussed replacing the DPW fuel tanks against a fuel card program; members agreed to gather more information before Town Meeting.
Health insurance was budgeted on an assumed increase, but the rate range is now capped lower, with the renewal due at the end of February.
A resident questioned putting free cash into OPEB; members defended the contribution as a sign of taking the liability seriously.
No votes on the budget were taken; the next meeting is set for February 21st with the council on aging, library and land use.

why_it_matters: The FY20 budget sets most of the town's spending and the tax bill that follows, and the schools are the largest share of the increase.
The fuel tank choice is a capital cost that Town Meeting may be asked to fund, so the comparison with a fuel card program could change what voters are asked to approve.
watch_next: February 21st meeting: council on aging, library and land use budgets.
Information on the fuel card alternative, due before Town Meeting.
